referred_to_by.content: A correction to what this record is. Until 2026-09-22 this collection recorded 'The Auction as Artwork' as a titled work, and modelled the two works around the 2009 engagement as its parts. The studio has stated that there was never a work of that title: the works are WTF is Ansel Adams and www.wtfisart.com, and the auction as artwork is the concept they share. The records agree with the studio. The phrase first appears in this collection on 2026-07-10, in the commit that first modelled the engagement, and no dated document uses it - not the 2008 and 2009 correspondence, not the private message of 2010, not the postings of 2011 and 2012, not the studio's archived websites, and not the 2013 letter to a university museum, which calls the sale 'a performance act of Metaconceptual Art' and gives it no title at all. The title was therefore this collection's, introduced by its data model, and not the artist's. The record keeps its identifier, because that identifier has been published, cited and archived, and is retyped from a made object to a concept. Two consequences follow. The origin claim for 2009 now names www.wtfisart.com as its work, the better dated of the two, whose name the registrar dates to 2009-03-16, fourteen days before the sale; WTF is Ansel Adams is recorded as the related work. And nothing about what is evidenced changes: the concept remains the studio's assertion, and its earliest dated statement is now a private message of 2010-04-12, dated by Facebook's servers, in which the studio principal calls the sale 'an act of contemporary conceptual art' and gives it no title.

The letter that gives the auction no title gives two other works one. The correction above rests in part on the 2013 letter to a university museum, which describes the sale as 'a performance act of Metaconceptual Art' and gives it no title. That is worth more than an absence, because the same letter titles other work in the same breath: 'Two popular examples of Metaconceptual Art, which are ongoing through time and space as well, are titled "Art Market Reform" , and "Art Tax"'. So the writer was naming works when he had names for them, in his own words, four years after the sale, and did not name this one. The argument for this record is therefore not only that no document uses the phrase 'The Auction as Artwork'; it is that the one document in which the studio lists its titled works, and mentions the auction, titles the works and not the auction.

A concept of Sun & Rain Works, and not a work, formed in connection with the Sotheby's Photographs auction of 2009 (sale N08533, New York), at which Sun & Rain Works consigned an Ansel Adams photograph, 'San Francisco from Twin Peaks' (lot 16). Following the logic of the readymade, Sun & Rain Works frames its engagement with that public institutional event — its mechanism of value, authority, and sale — as the material of art. This is a designation asserted by the artist and made explicit over time; it is not a publicly witnessed live-creation event, and the Sotheby's catalogue does not name Sun & Rain Works. The concept is realised in two works, the website www.wtfisart.com and WTF is Ansel Adams; it is not itself a titled work, and the correction above sets out how this collection came to record it as one.

Documentation reported by Sun & Rain Works includes 2008 correspondence with Sotheby's Photographs, the public catalogue lot, photographs, receipts, and related records; these evidence the artist identity and the consignment. The fuller archive remains held by the studio pending redaction and rights review. This record makes no adjudicated historical-priority claim and asserts no comparison with, or precedence over, any later artist or event absent separately published evidence.
